subject: Logic
title: Neglecting Sample Size
description: A short lesson to help you apply Neglecting Sample Size.

hook.text: A small hospital reports 70% boy births one month. A large one reports 52%. Which is more surprising?

buildup.text: Small samples are naturally more variable. A few births can easily swing to 70%. Thousands can't.

discovery.text: People treat small and large samples as equally reliable. They're not—small ones are noisier.

twist.text: A restaurant with five 5-star reviews isn't necessarily better than one with 500 reviews averaging 4.5.

climax.text: Always ask: how big is the sample? Small numbers can produce wild results by pure chance.

quiz.question: Why are small samples misleading?
options: They always show the true average
They have much higher natural variability
